notes.text: The sheet opens with the continuation “d'où”. No separate author title, author page number, date, or explicit author question is visible. The pencil 34 at lower left is retained as an archive-sheet comment.

The opening block contains the written complement expression for Sigma_12, then the wording “signifierait que”, a coproduct display for X, and two displayed pair definitions. These surrounding expressions prompted inspection of the separators and the negative-member subscript, but all visible older strokes and the remaining uncertainty are retained.

The annotation below the second member of Pi_1 carries two short vertical parallel marks and the written negative-member identity. Its live subscript reads 1. The older subscript, top horizontal at X, and low horizontal beside the separator remain uncertain. H's explicit note about rewriting of the subscript was considered.

The live equality after the cancelled Pi reads Pi_1 = Pi_3. The preceding displayed pair labels Pi_1 and Pi_2 supplied a mathematical cue to inspect the last numeral, while the crop supports the written 3. The connective is “alors”, and the mark after “contrairement” consists of two separated points.

The underlined cancelled heading Corollaire has Proposition written above it. The proposition text contains the uncertain Soit/Soient ending, a semicolon, “mutuellement non panachées”, an underlined “unique”, and two separate vertical emphasis strokes. The first ordered-pair exponent is T-shaped; comparison with the neighbouring plus leaves the flattened-plus alternative open.

The lower block writes C = Pi_1 amalg Pi_2 = omega_1 amalg omega_2 and describes four elements. It then gives a canonical application and its four displayed Sigma values. The target P style and its subscript remain uncertain from scan035 alone; the C context reference to another page was not followed.

The displayed labels (18) and (19) retain readable older last digits 7 and 8. The inline (18) retains a doubtful older 7. At (17) I could read 1 and a crossed 7 but could not identify a separate earlier numeral; no numbering history is supplied beyond the ink.

The final line visibly begins “et laquelle” and ends “injective, i.e.”. The syntactic cue toward à was considered without changing the observed et. No following page was read, and the continuation was not supplied.

No proof check, independent re-proof, computation, or formal certificate was performed. Mathematical context was used only to choose loci for close visual inspection and to report tensions between the written symbols and nearby labels.

workflow_feedback: Read reader_brief_v07, notation_before_scan035, packet.json, C, H, C_context, C_doubt_index, supplied C preamble, and H style instructions before the image sequence.
Viewed the whole image once for layout, then half a once and half b once line by line; no whole or half was re-enlarged or reopened.
Listed genuinely unresolved loci, made one crop for each coherent passage, and viewed each of the 15 crops once. No repeat crop was made.

Crops were made from the whole original with LANCZOS at 3000 pixels width, autocontrast, and UnsharpMask. No rotation was needed. No target clipping was observed; irrelevant adjacent-line strokes can reach a context-crop edge.
The complete reading.tex was saved immediately after image reading finished, and its availability was reported before this detailed JSON was composed.

All 20 supplied C doubt IDs have retained or resolved findings. Clear differences settled from halves also have original-image bounds. No finding phrase wraps to the opposite page edge; component boxes are supplied in the inventory for the long wrapped text blocks and separated display labels.
No OCR, recognition, PDF text extraction, external research, compilation, other-page inspection, other-reader inspection, or root-decision inspection was performed.
No proof-check event is claimed. Uncertainty-only comparisons with unchanged H primary text have against_H=false; H editorial notes were read for revision state and emphasis.
The two vertical margin marks are source emphasis strokes represented as rules. No separate drawing or diagram occurs on this page.
